bypass_all.$comment: --trust rides this preset, never the default launch argv: it does not just enable Multicode's own .grok/hooks agent-state reporter — it trusts EVERY project-level .grok config, including hooks committed in the repo itself, so a freshly cloned untrusted repo must not get it under the safe default. Without trust Grok skips project hooks and agent status falls back to output-timing inference (recoverable); the user can grant trust in the TUI via /hooks-trust.
bypass_all.label: Bypass all approvals (dangerous)

promptInjection.$comment: Grok Build's interactive TUI documents no positional prompt argument (headless -p is a one-shot, not a session). The pattern (?!) never matches by design: Grok's real input-ready marker is unknown, and any guessable pattern (e.g. the brand name) matches the startup banner before the TUI accepts input — injecting there both swallows the keystrokes and cancels the timeout fallback, while a post-timeout late match would inject a second copy. Never-match makes delivery deterministic: exactly one injection, via the runtime's timeout fallback, after the TUI has had timeoutMs to become ready. If a real install confirms `grok "prompt"` works interactively (Claude Code parity), flip mode to positional-arg — config-only change.

capabilities.$comment: resumeSession is intentionally false pending end-to-end verification (the MC-1464/MC-1465 discipline: an unverified resume path must not risk a lost conversation). Grok Build documents claude-style resume (-s/--session-id at launch, -r/--resume <id> on relaunch) and the resume argv above is wired for it, so once resume is verified against a real Grok Build install, flip this to true — no code change needed. sessionIdFromCaller is true because launch passes our minted --session-id.
